questions.title: Which party will receive the largest share of the vote in Berlin's 2026 state election?
questions.background: Berlin is both a city and a German federal state. Its state election determines the composition of its parliament.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results published by Berlin's election authority or reliable contemporaneous reporting of those results. Resolution : Resolve to the party receiving the highest statewide vote share in Berlin's 2026 state election. Subsequent coalition negotiations and the selection of the mayor do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The party's name or its standard abbreviation.
questions.current_reasoning: Major polling shift less than four weeks before Berlin's Sept 20 Abgeordnetenhaus election. A brand-new Forsa/t-online poll published Aug 22 (n=1,535, fielded Aug 4-18) puts Die Linke (led by Elif Eralp) clearly in first place at 22%, four points ahead of tied CDU (18%, lead candidate Stefan Evers; governing CDU-SPD coalition down to 30%) and AfD (18%), with Greens at 16% and SPD at 12%. An Aug 14 INSA/BILD poll (n=1,000) similarly showed a dead heat at the top: CDU 20%, Die Linke 19%, AfD 17% (down from leading at 19% in July 23 INSA), Greens 16%, SPD 15%. Ipsos (Aug 20) highlights extreme late volatility (52% of Berlin voters considering 2+ parties, voter potential 31-33% across Greens/SPD/CDU/Linke, 20% AfD). Heavy-tailed multi-party polling error modeling across Forsa/INSA (accounting for house effects, Die Linke's 2025 Berlin federal win, CDU's incumbent turnout base, and potential Saxony-Anhalt Sept 6 spillover for AfD) flips Die Linke into #1 (0.38, up from 0.12) ahead of CDU (0.33, down from 0.46), AfD (0.17), Alliance 90/The Greens (0.09), and SPD (0.03).
